name: CIFAR-10
description: CIFAR-10 is one of the most popular datasets in machine learning, containing 60,000 32x32 color images, each labeled as one of ten classes. It is divided into a training set of 50,000 images and a validation set of 10,000 images.
creator: Alex Krizhevsky, Vinod Nair, and Geoffrey Hinton
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images are normalized using CIFAR_MEAN = (0.4914, 0.4822, 0.4465) and CIFAR_STD = (0.2470, 0.2435, 0.2616). Images are converted from uint8 to half precision (fp16) and divided by 255. Images are permuted to channels_last memory format. For data augmentation, random horizontal flipping is used alongside 2-pixel random translation with reflection padding. A patch-whitening transformation is applied to the first convolutional layer, initialized as the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix of 2x2 patches across the training distribution.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset is used for training neural networks to reach 94% accuracy in 3.29 seconds, 95% in 10.4 seconds, and 96% in 46.3 seconds on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU. The training methods are intended to accelerate experimental iteration time for researchers working on compatible projects involving CIFAR-10 and to decrease the cost of projects involving a massive number of trained networks.
